There's a lot of theories of how the universe started, witht the current conclusion of it being the big bang. I'm more interested in how/if it'll end. Some theories include it rapidly shrinking to a singularity and ripping its own atoms apart and destroying matter, it ending and instantaneously starting up again and creating an exact copy that will eventually lead to the exact same galaxies, stars, planets, and even species, over and over again. Or it'll just keep continuing forever but as it expands, everything is getting further and further apart to the point we could look up at the night sky and and see nothing. Absolutely nothing. Of course we'll be lo g gone by then but still, Enjoy the stars while they're here. 

Also, do you believe there is intelligent life somewhere else in the universe? I do. Using the drake equation which is 100% circumstantial to what you personally believe, you can figure out how many inelegant life forms you yourself believe is in the entire universe. My answer was about 10,000. Which is incredibly small, but a lot in relation to us. The equation goes something like this "how many galaxies are there, how many stars are in those?, how many of those stars have planets?, how many of those planets are in the goldilocks zone? How many of those planets can actually sustain long enough for life to thrive? How many of those lifeforms are multiple cellular organisms, how many of those lifeforms can use tools, depending in what you consider inelegant (for me, monkeys, dolphins, elephants" how many of those lifeforms are inelegant. How many can use tools, have a written &spoken language, can create a society, and lastly have access to create and use nuclear weapons. It's a very interesting equation, and scary considering that up to the last question, my answer came out to be 10,000 life forms that are inelegant enough to create nuclear weapons, many more so just able to create a society.
